name: Threshold-activated discount
description:
Adds a third discount variant to the Sales pricing model — a percentage discount that activates only when a product's price strictly exceeds a configured `Money` threshold. The new value object `ThresholdDiscount` lives next to the existing `PercentageDiscount` and `ValueDiscount`; the `Discount` discriminated union is taught to host all three variants behind one caller-facing surface so existing call sites keep working unchanged.

Implementation notes. Every discount, `Discount` included, is an immutable C# `readonly struct` annotated with `[DddValueObject]`: equal by value (`IEquatable<T>` with `Equals(object?)`, `GetHashCode()` and a `ToString()` consistent across the variants), built only through a static factory behind a private constructor, and exposing no public getters — equality, `ApplyOn(Money)` and `ToString()` are its only observable behaviours. `ThresholdDiscount` lives in `Sales.DeepModel.Pricing.Discounts` next to `PercentageDiscount` and `ValueDiscount` and mirrors their shape. All three implement the existing `PriceModifier` interface in the same folder, which this design does not model as a building block: it carries no `[Ddd*]` annotation, so the scanned domain model leaves it out. `PercentageDiscount`, `ValueDiscount` and the `Discount.Percentage` and `Discount.Value` factories already exist and do not change; they are added here only so this green-field design shows the whole discounts module and the union has a complete picture. Only `Sales.Pricing.Discounts` is designed; the other `Sales` modules are out of scope.

description.value: Trigger: `ThresholdDiscount.Of(Percentage value, Money threshold)` is invoked. Pre-conditions: `value` and `threshold` are present. Algorithm: 1. The `Percentage` value object guarantees `value` lies within `[0%, 100%]` — no additional check is performed here (delegate, do not duplicate). 2. Inspect `threshold`: if it is non-positive (≤ zero in its currency), reject construction with a clear domain error indicating the threshold must be strictly positive. 3. If both checks pass, build the immutable instance via the private constructor and return it. Post-conditions: every existing instance has a percentage in `[0%, 100%]` and a strictly positive threshold; apply-time code can rely on this without re-checking. Edge cases: a zero threshold is rejected; a negative threshold is rejected; the rejection happens at the factory boundary so no invalid instance ever escapes.
description.author: agent

description.value: Trigger: `ApplyOn(price)` is called on a constructed `ThresholdDiscount`. Pre-conditions: the instance is valid by construction (percentage in range, threshold strictly positive). Algorithm: 1. Evaluate the predicate `price > threshold` using strict greater-than. 2. If true, compute and return `price * (Percentage.Of100 - value)` — same reduction formula as `PercentageDiscount.ApplyOn`. 3. If false, return `price` unchanged. Post-conditions: when the predicate is true, the result is the price reduced by the configured percentage; when false, the result equals the input price. Edge cases: `price == threshold` returns the price unchanged — the comparison is strict, matching the worked example (500 PLN at a 500-PLN threshold yields 500 PLN). A `0`-PLN threshold is not constructible (rejected by the factory), so the activation predicate cannot be trivially satisfied by a zero-threshold instance.

description.value: Private three-valued discriminator distinguishing the `Percentage`, `Value`, `Threshold` cases; it replaces the two-valued (bool) one that sufficed for two variants. Implementation choice (private nested enum or three named constants) is local; the rule is that dispatch over the discriminator must be exhaustive. The field is private — never observed by callers.
description.author: agent

description.value: Trigger: any operation on a `Discount` value that dispatches by variant — `ApplyOn(Money)`, `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `ToString`. Pre-conditions: the `Discount` is valid by construction (built through one of the three public static factories `Discount.Percentage`, `Discount.Value`, `Discount.Threshold`). Algorithm: 1. The discriminator field is a three-valued enum-like state — every dispatch must cover all three branches. 2. For each operation, route to the corresponding underlying value object: percentage variant → `_percentageDiscount`; value variant → `_valueDiscount`; threshold variant → `_thresholdDiscount`. 3. The non-active variant fields are at their default values and must not be observed. Post-conditions: every dispatch yields a single deterministic answer; no fallthrough or default branch is ever taken because the discriminator's three states cover every constructible `Discount`. Edge cases: introducing a fourth variant in the future would require updating every dispatch site — the rule mandates that an exhaustive switch (or equivalent) is used, not an `if/else` cascade that silently ignores an unknown discriminator value.
description.author: agent

description.value: Trigger: any change to the `Discount` type that touches its factory surface. Pre-conditions: the existing public static factories `Discount.Percentage(Percentage value)` and `Discount.Value(Money value)` exist and have known signatures relied upon by call sites across the solution. Algorithm: 1. The two existing factory methods MUST keep their exact current signatures and observable behaviour. 2. New variants are added via additional public static factories (here: `Discount.Threshold(Percentage value, Money threshold)`); they do not replace, rename, or alter the existing two. 3. The internal discriminator implementation is allowed to change (e.g. bool → enum-like) provided this stability rule for the public factories is preserved. Post-conditions: existing call sites compile and behave identically; the only API surface change visible to callers is the new factory. Edge cases: any rename or signature change of the existing factories is treated as a breaking change and is out of scope of this design doc.
description.author: agent

added.name: A Discount always holds exactly one valid discount

description.value: A `Discount` is made only by one of its factories, and only from a discount that could itself be made: when the underlying discount is rejected, the rejection reaches the caller and no `Discount` exists, never a partly made one. The kinds of discount it does not hold are never observed.
